purpose: The single machine-readable statement of what the pinned oracle image installs. scripts/verify-oracle-versions.mjs reads oracleVersions and fails when a validation record cites a version this image does not install, which is a check that needs no oracle present and therefore runs anywhere.
platformReason: conda-forge's PDAL stops at 2.7.2 for linux-aarch64. The version the corpus cites, 2.10.2, exists for linux-64 only, so the image is linux/amd64 and runs under emulation on an arm64 host.

baseImage.note: The Dockerfile pins the platform-specific manifest digest, not the tag and not the index.

oracleVersionsNote: Keyed by the oracle id scripts/verify-oracle-versions.mjs uses. GDAL is the version libgdal-core reports, which is what gdalinfo, gdaldem, gdal_translate, gdal_contour and ogrinfo all come from. A value may be a single version or a declared set of accepted versions; the verifier accepts a recorded version that matches any entry and still fails on one that matches none.
GDALVersionsNote: GDAL is a declared SET, not a single pin. The pinned image installs 3.13.1 (see condaPinned.gdal), and that is the canonical version most of the corpus was produced against. Four reference-run sets — validation/change-pair/reference-runs.json, validation/repeatability/antiochia-flight/reference-runs.json, and validation/cross-implementation/profile/reference-runs-profile-{section,endcap}.json — were produced on the reference workstation after its Homebrew GDAL was upgraded from 3.13.1 to 3.13.3, and truthfully record 3.13.3. Both are patch releases of GDAL 3.13.x and the studies that cite them pass their tolerances; the versions are recorded as they actually were rather than relabelled. 3.13.1 remains the version to reproduce against from the pinned image; 3.13.3 is declared so those honest host-produced records are not flagged as undeclared drift. Any GDAL version outside this set is still a failure.

laszip.reason: laspy's LASzip backend needs these Python bindings, which conda-forge does not package; conda-forge's laszip is the C++ library. laspy 2.7.0 constrains the extra to >=0.3.0,<0.4.0.

npm.nodeVersionReason: 3d-tiles-validator@0.6.1 pulls better-sqlite3@11.10.0 transitively. That package has no prebuilt binary for Node 26 and falls back to a node-gyp build that fails, so Node is 22.
npm.isolationReason: A separate manifest from the project's own package.json. An oracle must never enter the application's dependency tree, its lockfile or its SBOM.

whiteboxTools.versionsDisagree: The wrapper is 2.3.6 and the binary reports 2.4.0. The binary is what computes, so its own --version string is the identity that belongs in a record.

avoidedDownload.why: The whitebox wrapper fetches this on first import. The URL carries no version and no checksum, the downloader verifies no hash, and pinning whitebox==2.3.6 pins only the wrapper. The conda package is built from source and its sha256 is in the lock, so the image never reaches this URL.

observedHeaders.note: Recorded from a HEAD request as evidence that the artifact behind the versionless URL does change. It is not a checksum and is not used to verify anything.

avoidedDownload.upstreamReleasesHaveNoAssets: github.com/jblindsay/whitebox-tools releases v2.0.0 through v2.4.0 carry no binary assets at all, so there is no versioned download to pin instead.

settings.why: settings.json lives beside the executable and persists compress_rasters (default true) and max_procs (default -1). Both change output bytes. The copy shipped inside the Python package carries the upstream author's own home directory as working_directory.
settings.maxProcsCaveat: WhiteboxTools applies --max_procs per tool rather than globally, so max_procs=1 has to be verified for each tool a study uses rather than assumed from this file.
settings.wrapperCaveat: The Python wrapper reads settings.json from the current working directory at construction time, not from beside the executable, and it coerces verbose_mode with str(), which makes the string "False" truthy. A reference run should leave no settings.json in its working directory.

whiteboxTools.wbtPathCaveat: WBT_PATH only makes the wrapper skip its download. It does not redirect execution: the wrapper sets its executable directory to its own package directory and chdirs there before running ./whitebox_tools, so the image also links the binary into that directory.

lazBackends.independenceNote: lazrs and WhiteboxTools both wrap laz-rs, the same upstream decoder, so a laspy-with-lazrs result compared against WhiteboxTools is one implementation compared against itself. Only a run that used the LASzip backend can carry a cross-implementation claim, which is why record-oracle-versions.mjs records which backend was available and which one laspy picked.

GRASS.reason: conda-forge's grass 8.5.0 requires proj >=9.7.1,<9.8.0 and resolves against libgdal-core 3.12.3. The GDAL pin this corpus needs, 3.13.1, requires proj >=9.8.1,<9.9.0. The two cannot share one environment, so GRASS would have to be a second prefix or a second image.
GRASS.sizeCost: A GRASS-only linux-64 solve is 171 packages and 260 MB of downloads.

CloudCompare.status: off by default, opt in with --build-arg WITH_CLOUDCOMPARE=1
CloudCompare.headlessVerified: Tested in this image on 2026-08-22. CloudCompare -SILENT -AUTO_SAVE OFF -O a.txt -O b.txt -C2C_DIST over two 200-point clouds under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, with no X server and no xvfb, exited 0 and reported a mean distance of 0.303472.
CloudCompare.cost: 200 packages, 149 MiB of .debs. The installed size delta was not measured.
CloudCompare.pinWeakness: apt resolves against whatever trixie serves today, which is a weaker pin than the hash-verified conda, PyPI and npm installs. Pin the deb versions from snapshot.debian.org before a study depends on it.

SAGA.reason: One study, VRM-SAGA-ANALYTIC, used SAGA 7.8.2 from a QGIS bundle. conda-forge has no saga package, so this image cannot reproduce that leg. The guard reports SAGA as absent rather than failing.

R.reason: MEAS-PROFILE-OGR-R-CORRIDOR used R 4.4.1 and SpatiaLite 5.1.0. Both are packaged by conda-forge and could be added, at the cost of a separate solve, because r-base pulls a large dependency set of its own.
